title: THE QUICK PEOPLE OF THE PULSAR
deck: Around the pulsar Wend-9, a plasma civilization that thinks a quarter of a million times faster than humans is walling off the hydrogen three hundred people need to breathe. Illuminara has fifteen days, a station that has been shouting a day-long sentence every six days of their time, and a rival physicist whose model fits the same numbers.
shape: Five scenes across five days: a lattice found in forgotten raw data, a ruler laid across an unbearable cadence, a sealed table that lets both explanations lose, a seven-second quiet in which a gate opens on the predicted clock while the strongest physical rival is starved, and two doors from which the quick people choose their own pause.

scenes.title: Noise at Four Microseconds
paragraphs: *Wend-9 Station, observation ring · Day One, 06:40*

Three hundred people lived on Wend-9 Station, and every morning the torus around the pulsar let them have a little less of its hydrogen. The scoop on the station's leading edge had drunk eighty-one units a day for six years. It drank twenty-seven now, thirty-four percent of what it was built for, and the figure fell by three points with every morning.
Director Idris Maule laid it out beside the long window, where the plasma ring hung around a star too small to see. Hydrogen fed the fuel cells, the water, and the shuttle's one return burn.

**Idris Maule**  
Reserve is twenty-two days at full draw, and the burn line is eight. At this rate I reach it on Day Sixteen. I sign the evacuation on Day Fifteen or I don't sign it. I would like to know what I am signing.

**Illuminara**  
Tell me about the noise.
Dr. Lenka Voss did not wait for the director.

**Lenka Voss**  
It is not a message, and I would put my name on that. The torus rings at point five two hertz. We range the orbit at point five oh. Drive a resonator near its mode and it rings back, and the field piles into a ridge where the ringing is strongest. The ridge is your shield. The replies are the ringdown, with a four-millisecond texture, because that is what plasma does.

Illuminara asked who had looked at the recordings and at what speed. Beatriz Okonjo, who ran communications and kept the baseband recorder because no one else remembered it, put up her hand like a schoolgirl.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
The summary the physicists read is sampled at one kilohertz. The recorder underneath takes ten million samples a second. It writes to cold storage and nobody opens it.

**Illuminara**  
Then they have been listening to a book through a fan. Show me the raw.
The screen filled with spikes. Beatriz laid a ruler of faint lines across them and the spikes sat on it like swifts on a wire.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Four microseconds. Every burst lands on that grid, give or take a tenth. After each of our chirps there is one burst, a hundred and twenty-seven steps long.

**Illuminara**  
Our chirp is a hundred and twenty-seven chips.

**Lenka Voss**  
Which smear to fifty milliseconds in the summary and look like ringing. A coincidence of code length is not a language.

**Illuminara**  
No. It is a rule I can fail. Half a millisecond is the length of a sneeze. If it is a sentence, it is one the station has been answering with a shout.

scenes.title: The Ruler
paragraphs: *Wend-9 Station, wardroom · Day One, 14:10*

She wrote the arithmetic on the wardroom table in grease pencil so that nobody could say it had been done out of sight. She called it a ruler, not a fact, and drew one tick of theirs as one second of a human mind, to be thrown away the day it failed to predict anything.

**Illuminara**  
The station's ranging chirp lasts four tenths of a second. At a quarter of a million ticks per second, that is a hundred thousand ticks. By my ruler it is twenty-eight hours of unbroken pressure. Then one point six seconds of quiet, four and a half days. Then it starts again, every two seconds, five and three-quarter days, with the same bruise.

**Ansel Tarkov**  
You are asking me to believe that plasma has a grievance with our contract.

**Illuminara**  
I am asking you to watch a ruler break. If it breaks, I will say so on this table. They answered every chirp, Mr. Tarkov, and we answered their answers with the next chirp. To them we are a weather system that never stops and never listens.
Tarkov was the consortium's liaison, and the ranging data was his budget line. He folded his hands over it as if it might leave.

**Lenka Voss**  
Your point five two is my resonance. You cannot take my number and call it your argument.

**Illuminara**  
It is the same number with two readings. You say it is how fast the torus rings. I say it is how long it takes for one thought to go once around the ring and come back as agreement, a council of a thousand voices that cannot decide anything shorter than one circuit. One point nine two seconds. We chirp at two. We interrupt them just before they finish every sentence they start.

**Idris Maule**  
And how do we tell which of you is right before Day Fifteen?

**Illuminara**  
By asking where you disagree, and going there first.

scenes.title: Sealed Table
paragraphs: *Wend-9 Station, wardroom · Day Two, 09:00*

They built the table together, and it took three hours because Voss insisted on writing her own column and Illuminara insisted that hers be allowed to lose. Two hypotheses went down the left side. The tests ran across the top.

**Lenka Voss**  
Control. We chirp at two seconds for six hours. Both of us say the shield narrows three points a day. If either of us says otherwise, the table is worthless.

**Illuminara**  
Agreed. Second, a single chirp, then one second of quiet, then back to the cadence. Half a circuit. I say the gate cannot open and the closure continues. You say the ridge relaxes, two points of intake come back.

**Lenka Voss**  
Third, one chirp and seven seconds of quiet. The torus relaxes smoothly, an e-fold in eleven seconds. A ramp. And the ringdown replays your code with the same sign, each pass half as large.

**Illuminara**  
I say a gate. Nothing for three point eight four seconds, two full circuits from the end of the chirp, one to decide and one to act, and then the seam opens. Sharp, four tenths of a second wide, a chirp's width. And a reply that is not a replay. A resonator cannot run a code backwards. I predict the reverse and complement of whatever we send.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Then it has to be a code that nobody on this station has ever seen, and nobody can see before it flies.

She drew it from a strontium source in the lab, a count of decays in a window, a hundred and twenty-seven bits that existed nowhere until the counter ticked. Ansel Tarkov did not approve and did not stop her.

**Ansel Tarkov**  
Every second of quiet is a second of ranging lost. I want it recorded that I objected.

**Idris Maule**  
It is recorded. The table is sealed. If the closure rate moves in the control, I want to hear it before I hear anything else.
Voss, Maule and Illuminara signed across the envelope flap, and Beatriz taped it to the wardroom wall where everyone could see that it had not moved.

scenes.title: Seven Seconds of Quiet
paragraphs: *Wend-9 Station, communications bay · Day Four, 11:12*

The control had behaved. On Day Three the closure had held at its three points a day, in both columns. The one-second quiet had gone the way Illuminara had said and not the way Voss had said: the intake stayed where it was, and the ridge did not relax. Voss had looked at it a long while and said nothing. Intake read twenty-two percent. The reserve stood at nineteen days.
Beatriz drew the code at 11:09. Maule stood behind her with the evacuation order folded in his pocket where he could feel its corners.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Chirp in ten. Nine.
The ranging laser fired its four tenths of a second and the room went quiet in a way the station never was. For the first time in six years nobody sent anything at all.

**Idris Maule**  
One second.

**Lenka Voss**  
Torus is ringing down. Exactly as I said.

**Illuminara**  
Keep counting.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Two seconds. Three.
The ringdown on the main screen began a smooth slope and Voss's mouth set. Then the slope stopped, as if the torus had put a hand flat on a table.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Three point eight, three point eight three, three point eight four.

The seam opened. Hydrogen, which had been a thread, poured into the scoop, a rectangle of intake the width of exactly one chirp. At 11:12:04 it stood at ninety-four percent for four tenths of a second and then shut, with the neatness of a door closed by someone who had finished their sentence.
A burst sat in the record, half a millisecond long, laid on the four-microsecond grid. Beatriz ran the correlation against the code from the strontium counter.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
It's the code. Reversed. And complemented, every bit. Aligned to a fifth of a microsecond.

**Lenka Voss**  
A linear resonator does not run backwards. That one is dead. A pumped one is another animal: a plasma mirror hands back the time-reverse of whatever hits it, and if its pump sits a half-turn out of phase, the complement comes free. I cannot rule that out from here.

**Illuminara**  
Then convict it or acquit it in a number.

**Lenka Voss**  
Lag. A mirror builds its reply out of the pump, and builds slowly when the pump is weak. Starve it and it is late. Something with a clock answers at the clock. Ten new codes, drawn by Beatriz, shown to no one: five at full power, five at a quarter, two of those at half length. If the gate slides past seven seconds on the weak ones, it was my mirror, and I want the ringdown back.

**Illuminara**  
You will have all ten. And if it comes back late, I will say mirror at this table, in grease pencil.

**Lenka Voss**  
I am the happiest woman on this station. Whichever of us loses, we are wrong in a direction no one has been wrong before.

scenes.title: The Pause They Gave Back
paragraphs: *Wend-9 Station, wardroom · Day Five, 08:30*

The ten had come back in the night. The gate had stood at three point eight four seconds at full power, and at a quarter power, and at half length, give or take a hundredth. Nothing had been late. Voss read the lag column standing, then sat and wrote under her own heading, in pencil, *mirror: late. It was not late.*

**Lenka Voss**  
That is not a someone. It is a clock I did not put there. You may call it a someone.

**Illuminara**  
I will call it the cheapest thing left.

The shield had come down to a low wall in the same hours, and the intake read seventy-one percent and did not move. It was not what the station had been built to take. It was what the quick people had decided to give.

**Idris Maule**  
Fifty-seven units a day come in at seventy-one. The station can live on forty-eight. I am cutting our draw from eighty-one to fifty-six, which holds the reserve flat at nineteen days, fifteen hundred and thirty-nine units. The burn line is six hundred and forty-eight. If the intake went to nothing tomorrow, that leaves eight hundred and ninety-one units above the line, sixteen days at fifty-six. The order comes back out if intake reads under forty-eight three days running, or the reserve falls under twelve days. A fresh one takes eleven minutes to print.

**Idris Maule**  
But I do not shred it on a gift whose terms we wrote ourselves. They have told us what they will share. Have they told us how often we may speak? Otherwise this is a schedule, and I know one when it arrives from the strong side of a table.

**Illuminara**  
Then they write the terms. Two doors, written down before anyone fires. They may take one, bend one, or leave both. Door A is twenty milliseconds, once a minute. By my ruler that is eighty-three minutes of pressure once in a hundred and seventy-four days, and Mr. Tarkov's orbit solution loosens from forty metres to two hundred and twenty. Door B is the same twenty milliseconds every ten seconds: eighty-three minutes every twenty-nine days, and Mr. Tarkov keeps his orbit to sixty metres and his tidal ripple.

**Ansel Tarkov**  
B. Obviously B.

**Illuminara**  
B is six times the weather. It is the door that suits us, which is why none of us chooses. The strontium counter orders the blocks, six minutes each. A door is theirs when the gate stands at three point eight four on every chirp in its block and the intake does not step down. A door is refused when a chirp goes unanswered and the intake steps down.

**Idris Maule**  
And if they take neither?

**Illuminara**  
Then the order stays in your pocket, you sign on Day Fifteen, and I help you write it.
Tarkov took his turn standing.

**Ansel Tarkov**  
And if they take B, I keep my paper?

**Illuminara**  
You keep your paper, and I will be a good deal more surprised than you. If they take A, you lose the ripple, and I cannot make that go away. You may refuse to fire A, and I will tell the director so. You wanted to be the man who got the first dialogue with another kind of mind, not the man who lost it for a paper.
Tarkov looked at the grease-pencil table for a long time, then signed it on the condition that both doors be offered again in ninety days.
The counter put B first. At 09:40 Beatriz fired twenty milliseconds, and Maule sat in front of a silent screen and counted.

**Idris Maule**  
Three point eight. Three point eight four.

The second chirp ten seconds later was answered on the same clock. The third was not. The seam stayed shut, the intake stepped from seventy-one to fifty-two and held there, and the room understood it had been told something without a word.

Fifty-two was forty-two units against a draw of fifty-six. Maule wrote the fourteen short in the margin of the order; the eight hundred and ninety-one above the line would carry that for sixty days. He did not look up from it.

**Idris Maule**  
That is a no.

**Illuminara**  
That is a door. Fire A.

In the second block the first chirp left the laser 0.7 seconds into a circuit of theirs, by Beatriz's clock, and the reply came with the seam shut and the tail doubled. The intake did not step down further. The next chirp she slaved to the start of the circuit, to the half-hertz beat of the torus, and was answered, and so was the next, and so were all six. From the second answer the intake climbed from fifty-two, and when the block ended it read seventy-one again and stayed there.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
They'll take A if we start where they start.

**Lenka Voss**  
My ring period. Naturally.

**Illuminara**  
They have told us where in the ring they begin to speak. The ruler does not have to choose between us, Dr. Voss. It is the same grid in both readings.
Maule watched the screen read seventy-one for a full quarter of an hour. Then he fed the folded order into the shredder himself, slowly, and it came out a hundred strips of identical width.

**Idris Maule**  
Seventy-one is a number I can live on. I would rather have a hundred.

**Illuminara**  
They did not offer a hundred. I would ask for nothing they have not offered.

**Ansel Tarkov**  
I lose two years of a paper.

**Illuminara**  
You do.

Every reply came with a tail on it, forty steps that had not been in the code. The tail was identical on every exchange that followed, and no one on the station could say whether it was a name, a title or a shrug.
Beatriz found the other thing at noon. After each reply the quick people left a silence of one point nine two seconds, one circuit of their ring, before the next possible word.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
They're waiting for us.

**Lenka Voss**  
Of course they are. They are polite. It is the longest anyone has ever waited for anyone. For them it was five and a half days.
Maule stayed at the screen until the quiet ran out, as it did every day after that, and the station answered.

critic_line: Illuminara turns an apparent resource siege into a falsifiable encounter, lets the quick people reject the cadence that benefits the station most, and earns a safe shared rhythm whose arithmetic, consent and human costs remain visible.

translation_sl.title: HITRI LJUDJE PULZARJA
translation_sl.deck: Okoli pulzarja Wend-9 plazemska civilizacija, ki razmišlja četrt milijonkrat hitreje od ljudi, zapira vodik, ki ga tristo ljudi potrebuje za dihanje. Illuminara ima petnajst dni, postajo, ki vsakih šest njihovih dni vpije en dan dolg stavek, ter tekmico fizičarko, katere model ustreza istim številkam.
translation_sl.shape: Pet prizorov v petih dneh: mreža, najdena v pozabljenih neobdelanih podatkih; ravnilo, položeno čez neznosen ritem; zapečatena tabela, ki obema razlagama omogoči poraz; sedemsekundna tišina, v kateri se vrata odprejo ob napovedanem času, medtem ko najmočnejši fizikalni tekmec ostane brez energije; ter dvoje vrat, med katerima hitri ljudje izberejo svoj premor.

scenes.title: Šum pri štirih mikrosekundah
paragraphs: *Postaja Wend-9, opazovalni obroč · Prvi dan, 06:40*

Na postaji Wend-9 je živelo tristo ljudi in vsako jutro jim je torus okoli pulzarja prepustil nekoliko manj svojega vodika. Zajemalnik na vodilnem robu postaje je šest let srkal enainosemdeset enot na dan. Zdaj jih je srkal sedemindvajset, štiriintrideset odstotkov načrtovane količine, številka pa je vsako jutro padla za tri točke.

Direktor Idris Maule je podatke razgrnil ob dolgem oknu, kjer je plazemski obroč visel okoli zvezde, premajhne, da bi jo videli. Vodik je napajal gorivne celice, vodo in edini povratni vžig raketoplana.

**Idris Maule**  
Zaloge zadoščajo za dvaindvajset dni pri polni porabi, meja za vžig pa je osem dni. Ob tej hitrosti jo dosežem šestnajsti dan. Petnajsti dan podpišem evakuacijo ali pa je ne podpišem. Rad bi vedel, kaj podpisujem.

**Illuminara**  
Povejte mi o šumu.
Dr. Lenka Voss ni čakala na direktorja.

**Lenka Voss**  
To ni sporočilo in za to bi zastavila svoje ime. Torus niha pri nič cela dvainpetdeset herca. Orbito merimo pri nič cela petdeset. Če resonator vzbujate blizu njegovega lastnega načina, zazveni nazaj, polje pa se nakopiči v greben tam, kjer je nihanje najmočnejše. Greben je vaš ščit. Odgovori so izzvenevanje s štirimilisekundno teksturo, ker se plazma tako vede.

Illuminara je vprašala, kdo je pregledal posnetke in pri kateri hitrosti. Beatriz Okonjo, ki je vodila zveze in ohranila snemalnik osnovnega pasu, ker se ga nihče drug ni spomnil, je dvignila roko kakor šolarka.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Povzetek, ki ga berejo fiziki, je vzorčen pri enem kilohercu. Snemalnik pod njim zajema deset milijonov vzorcev na sekundo. Piše v hladno shrambo in nihče je ne odpira.

**Illuminara**  
Potem so poslušali knjigo skozi ventilator. Pokažite mi neobdelane podatke.
Zaslon so preplavile konice. Beatriz je čeznje položila ravnilo iz medlih črt in konice so obsedle na njem kakor hudourniki na žici.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Štiri mikrosekunde. Vsak izbruh pristane na tej mreži, z odstopanjem največ desetinke. Po vsakem našem žvrgolenju pride en izbruh, dolg sto sedemindvajset korakov.

**Illuminara**  
Naše žvrgolenje ima sto sedemindvajset čipov.

**Lenka Voss**  
Ti se v povzetku razmažejo na petdeset milisekund in so videti kot nihanje. Naključno ujemanje dolžine kode ni jezik.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. To je pravilo, pri katerem se lahko zmotim. Pol milisekunde je dolžina kihanja. Če je to stavek, mu postaja odgovarja z vpitjem.

scenes.title: Ravnilo
paragraphs: *Postaja Wend-9, obednica · Prvi dan, 14:10*

Račun je z mastnim svinčnikom zapisala na mizo v obednici, da nihče ne bi mogel trditi, da je nastal skrit pred očmi. Imenovala ga je ravnilo, ne dejstvo, in eno njihovo tiktakanje narisala kot eno sekundo človeškega uma; zavreči ga je bilo treba tisti dan, ko ne bi več ničesar napovedalo.

**Illuminara**  
Merilno žvrgolenje postaje traja štiri desetinke sekunde. Pri četrt milijona tiktakov na sekundo je to sto tisoč tiktakov. Po mojem ravnilu je to osemindvajset ur neprekinjenega pritiska. Nato ena cela šest sekunde tišine, štiri dni in pol. Potem se začne znova, vsaki dve sekundi, vsakih pet dni in tri četrt, z isto modrico.

**Ansel Tarkov**  
Od mene pričakujete, da verjamem, da ima plazma zamero do naše pogodbe.

**Illuminara**  
Prosim vas, da opazujete, kako se ravnilo zlomi. Če se bo, bom to povedala za to mizo. Odgovorili so na vsako žvrgolenje, gospod Tarkov, mi pa smo na njihove odgovore odgovorili z naslednjim žvrgolenjem. Zanje smo vremenski sistem, ki se nikoli ne ustavi in nikoli ne posluša.
Tarkov je bil povezovalec konzorcija, podatki merjenja orbite pa njegova proračunska postavka. Čeznje je sklenil roke, kot da bi lahko odšli.

**Lenka Voss**  
Vaših nič cela dvainpetdeset je moja resonanca. Ne morete vzeti moje številke in jo razglasiti za svoj argument.

**Illuminara**  
To je ista številka z dvema razlagama. Vi pravite, da kaže, kako hitro torus niha. Jaz pravim, da kaže, koliko časa potrebuje ena misel, da enkrat obkroži obroč in se vrne kot soglasje, svet tisoč glasov, ki ne more ničesar odločiti hitreje kot v enem obhodu. Ena cela dvaindevetdeset sekunde. Mi žvrgolimo na dve. Prekinemo jih tik preden dokončajo vsak stavek, ki ga začnejo.

**Idris Maule**  
In kako pred petnajstim dnem ugotovimo, katera od vaju ima prav?

**Illuminara**  
Tako, da najprej poiščemo kraj, kjer se ne strinjata, in gremo tja.

scenes.title: Zapečatena tabela
paragraphs: *Postaja Wend-9, obednica · Drugi dan, 09:00*
Tabelo so sestavili skupaj, trajalo pa je tri ure, ker je Voss vztrajala, da napiše svoj stolpec, Illuminara pa, da sme njen stolpec izgubiti. Dve hipotezi sta zapisali na levi, preizkuse pa čez vrh.

**Lenka Voss**  
Kontrola. Šest ur žvrgolimo na dve sekundi. Obe praviva, da se ščit zoži za tri točke na dan. Če katera reče drugače, je tabela ničvredna.

**Illuminara**  
Dogovorjeno. Drugič: eno žvrgolenje, nato ena sekunda tišine, nato nazaj v ritem. Pol obhoda. Jaz pravim, da se vrata ne morejo odpreti in zapiranje se nadaljuje. Vi pravite, da greben popusti in se vrneta dve točki zajema.

**Lenka Voss**  
Tretjič: eno žvrgolenje in sedem sekund tišine. Torus se enakomerno sprošča, z e-časom enajstih sekund. Klančina. Izzvenevanje pa ponovi vašo kodo z istim predznakom, vsak obhod polovico šibkeje.

**Illuminara**  
Jaz pravim vrata. Tri cela štiriinosemdeset sekunde ničesar, dva polna obhoda od konca žvrgolenja, eden za odločitev in eden za dejanje, nato se šiv odpre. Ostro, štiri desetinke sekunde široko, toliko kot žvrgolenje. In odgovor, ki ni ponovitev. Resonator kode ne more predvajati nazaj. Napovedujem obrat in komplement vsega, kar pošljemo.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Potem mora biti to koda, ki je nihče na postaji še ni videl in je nihče ne more videti, preden poleti.

Izžrebala jo je iz stroncijevega vira v laboratoriju, iz števila razpadov v časovnem oknu, sto sedemindvajset bitov, ki niso obstajali nikjer, dokler ni števec odtiktakal. Ansel Tarkov tega ni odobraval, vendar je ni ustavil.

**Ansel Tarkov**  
Vsaka sekunda tišine je sekunda izgubljenega merjenja. Hočem, da je zapisano, da sem ugovarjal.

**Idris Maule**  
Zapisano je. Tabela je zapečatena. Če se stopnja zapiranja v kontroli premakne, hočem to slišati pred vsem drugim.
Voss, Maule in Illuminara so se podpisali čez zavihek ovojnice, Beatriz pa jo je prilepila na steno obednice, kjer so vsi lahko videli, da se ni premaknila.

scenes.title: Sedem sekund tišine
paragraphs: *Postaja Wend-9, komunikacijski oddelek · Četrti dan, 11:12*

Kontrola se je vedla po pričakovanjih. Tretji dan je zapiranje ostalo pri treh točkah na dan v obeh stolpcih. Enosekundna tišina se je razpletla, kakor je rekla Illuminara, in ne kakor je rekla Voss: zajem je ostal na istem, greben pa ni popustil. Voss je dolgo gledala podatke in molčala. Zajem je kazal dvaindvajset odstotkov. Zaloge so zadoščale za devetnajst dni.
Beatriz je kodo izžrebala ob 11:09. Maule je stal za njo, evakuacijski nalog pa je imel zložen v žepu, kjer je čutil njegove robove.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Žvrgolenje čez deset. Devet.
Merilni laser je sprožil svoje štiri desetinke sekunde in prostor je utihnil tako, kot postaja nikoli ni. Prvič v šestih letih nihče ni poslal ničesar.

**Idris Maule**  
Ena sekunda.

**Lenka Voss**  
Torus izzveneva. Točno tako, kot sem rekla.

**Illuminara**  
Štejte naprej.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Dve sekundi. Tri.
Izzvenevanje na glavnem zaslonu se je začelo spuščati po gladki krivulji in Voss je stisnila usta. Nato se je krivulja ustavila, kot da bi torus položil dlan na mizo.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Tri cela osem, tri cela triinosemdeset, tri cela štiriinosemdeset.

Šiv se je odprl. Vodik, ki je bil prej le nit, je planil v zajemalnik, pravokotnik dotoka, širok natanko toliko kot eno žvrgolenje. Ob 11:12:04 je štiri desetinke sekunde stal pri štiriindevetdesetih odstotkih, nato pa se zaprl tako urejeno kakor vrata, ki jih je zaprl nekdo, ki je dokončal svoj stavek.
V zapisu je sedel pol milisekunde dolg izbruh, položen na štirimikrosekundno mrežo. Beatriz je izračunala korelacijo s kodo iz stroncijevega števca.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
To je koda. Obrnjena. In komplementirana, vsak bit. Poravnana na petino mikrosekunde.

**Lenka Voss**  
Linearni resonator ne predvaja nazaj. Ta možnost je mrtva. Črpani resonator je druga žival: plazemsko zrcalo vrne časovni obrat vsega, kar ga zadene, in če je njegova črpalka za pol obrata zunaj faze, dobite komplement zastonj. Od tod tega ne morem izključiti.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ga obsodite ali oprostite s številko.

**Lenka Voss**  
Zakasnitev. Zrcalo zgradi odgovor iz črpalke in ga gradi počasi, kadar je črpalka šibka. Izstradajte ga in zamudi. Nekaj z uro odgovori ob času ure. Deset novih kod, ki jih izžreba Beatriz in jih ne pokaže nikomur: pet pri polni moči, pet pri četrtinski, od teh dve polovične dolžine. Če vrata pri šibkih zdrsnejo čez sedem sekund, je bilo moje zrcalo in hočem izzvenevanje nazaj.

**Illuminara**  
Dobili boste vseh deset. In če se vrne pozno, bom za to mizo z mastnim svinčnikom napisala zrcalo.

**Lenka Voss**  
Sem najsrečnejša ženska na tej postaji. Katera koli od naju izgubi, se motiva v smeri, v kateri se ni še nihče.

scenes.title: Premor, ki so ga vrnili
paragraphs: *Postaja Wend-9, obednica · Peti dan, 08:30*

Vseh deset odgovorov se je ponoči vrnilo. Vrata so stala pri treh celih štiriinosemdeset sekunde pri polni moči, četrtinski moči in polovični dolžini, z odstopanjem največ stotinke. Noben odgovor ni zamudil. Voss je stolpec zakasnitev prebrala stoje, nato sedla in s svinčnikom pod svoj naslov zapisala: *zrcalo: pozno. Ni bilo pozno.*

**Lenka Voss**  
To ni nekdo. To je ura, ki je nisem postavila jaz. Lahko jo imenujete nekdo.

**Illuminara**  
Imenovala jo bom najcenejša preostala razlaga.

V istih urah se je ščit spustil do nizkega zidu, zajem pa je kazal enainsedemdeset odstotkov in se ni več premikal. To ni bilo tisto, za kar je bila postaja zgrajena. Bilo je tisto, kar so hitri ljudje sklenili dati.

**Idris Maule**  
Pri enainsedemdesetih odstotkih priteče sedeminpetdeset enot na dan. Postaja lahko preživi z oseminštiridesetimi. Porabo zmanjšujem z enainosemdeset na šestinpetdeset, kar ohrani zalogo pri devetnajstih dneh, tisoč petsto devetintridesetih enotah. Meja za vžig je šeststo oseminštirideset. Če bi dotok jutri padel na nič, ostane nad mejo osemsto enaindevetdeset enot, šestnajst dni pri šestinpetdesetih. Nalog znova stopi v veljavo, če je dotok tri dni zapored pod oseminštirideset ali če zaloga pade pod dvanajst dni. Novega je mogoče natisniti v enajstih minutah.

**Idris Maule**  
Toda ne bom ga raztrgal zaradi daru, katerega pogoje smo napisali sami. Povedali so nam, koliko bodo delili. So povedali, kako pogosto smemo govoriti? Sicer je to urnik in enega prepoznam, ko pride z močnejše strani mize.

**Illuminara**  
Potem pogoje napišejo oni. Dvoje vrat, zapisanih, preden kdor koli sproži. Lahko vzamejo ena, ena spremenijo ali pustijo oboja. Vrata A so dvajset milisekund enkrat na minuto. Po mojem ravnilu je to triinosemdeset minut pritiska enkrat na sto štiriinsedemdeset dni, rešitev orbite gospoda Tarkova pa se razrahlja s štiridesetih metrov na dvesto dvajset. Vrata B so istih dvajset milisekund vsakih deset sekund: triinosemdeset minut vsakih devetindvajset dni, gospod Tarkov pa ohrani orbito na šestdesetih metrih in svoj plimski val.

**Ansel Tarkov**  
B. Očitno B.

**Illuminara**  
B je šestkrat več vremena. To so vrata, ki ustrezajo nam, zato nihče od nas ne izbira. Stroncijev števec razvrsti šestminutne bloke. Vrata so njihova, kadar so vrata ob vsakem žvrgolenju pri treh celih štiriinosemdeset sekunde in dotok ne pade. Vrata so zavrnjena, kadar žvrgolenje ostane brez odgovora in dotok pade.

**Idris Maule**  
In če ne vzamejo nobenih?

**Illuminara**  
Potem nalog ostane v vašem žepu, petnajsti dan ga podpišete, jaz pa vam ga pomagam napisati.
Tarkov je vstal, ko je prišel na vrsto.

**Ansel Tarkov**  
In če izberejo B, obdržim svoj članek?

**Illuminara**  
Obdržite ga, mene pa bo precej bolj presenetilo kot vas. Če izberejo A, izgubite plimski val in tega ne morem odpraviti. Lahko zavrnete sprožitev A in to bom povedala direktorju. Hoteli ste biti človek, ki je dosegel prvi dialog z drugo vrsto uma, ne človek, ki ga je izgubil zaradi članka.
Tarkov je dolgo gledal tabelo z mastnim svinčnikom, nato pa jo podpisal pod pogojem, da bodo oboja vrata znova ponudili čez devetdeset dni.
Števec je najprej določil B. Ob 09:40 je Beatriz sprožila dvajset milisekund, Maule pa je sedel pred molčečim zaslonom in štel.

**Idris Maule**  
Tri cela osem. Tri cela štiriinosemdeset.

Drugo žvrgolenje deset sekund pozneje je dobilo odgovor ob istem času. Tretje ga ni. Šiv je ostal zaprt, dotok je padel z enainsedemdeset na dvainpetdeset in tam obstal, soba pa je razumela, da ji je bilo nekaj povedano brez besede.

Dvainpetdeset odstotkov je pomenilo dvainštirideset enot proti porabi šestinpetdeset. Maule je na rob naloga zapisal primanjkljaj štirinajstih; osemsto enaindevetdeset enot nad mejo bi ga pokrilo šestdeset dni. Ni dvignil pogleda.

**Idris Maule**  
To je ne.

**Illuminara**  
To so vrata. Sprožite A.

V drugem bloku je prvo žvrgolenje zapustilo laser nič cela sedem sekunde po začetku njihovega obhoda po Beatrizini uri, odgovor pa je prišel z zaprtim šivom in podvojenim repom. Dotok ni več padel. Naslednje žvrgolenje je uskladila z začetkom obhoda, s polherčnim utripom torusa, in dobilo je odgovor; prav tako naslednje in vseh šest. Od drugega odgovora je dotok naraščal z dvainpetdeset in ob koncu bloka znova kazal enainsedemdeset ter tam ostal.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Vzeli bodo A, če začnemo tam, kjer začnejo oni.

**Lenka Voss**  
Moja obhodna doba. Seveda.

**Illuminara**  
Povedali so nam, kje v obroču začnejo govoriti. Ravnilu ni treba izbirati med nama, dr. Voss. V obeh razlagah je ista mreža.
Maule je četrt ure opazoval zaslon pri enainsedemdesetih. Nato je zložen nalog sam počasi spustil v rezalnik in iz njega je prišlo sto enako širokih trakov.

**Idris Maule**  
Enainsedemdeset je številka, s katero lahko živim. Raje bi imel sto.

**Illuminara**  
Sto niso ponudili. Ne bi prosila za nič, česar niso ponudili.

**Ansel Tarkov**  
Izgubim dve leti članka.

**Illuminara**  
Jih.
Vsak odgovor je imel rep, štirideset korakov, ki jih v kodi ni bilo. Rep je bil pri vseh nadaljnjih izmenjavah enak in nihče na postaji ni mogel reči, ali je ime, naziv ali skomig.
Beatriz je opoldne našla še nekaj. Po vsakem odgovoru so hitri ljudje pustili eno celo dvaindevetdeset sekunde tišine, en obhod svojega obroča, preden je bila mogoča naslednja beseda.

**Beatriz Okonjo**  
Čakajo nas.

**Lenka Voss**  
Seveda. Vljudni so. To je najdaljše čakanje kogar koli na kogar koli. Zanje je trajalo pet dni in pol.
Maule je ostal pri zaslonu, dokler se tišina ni iztekla, kakor se je vsak dan zatem, postaja pa je odgovorila.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara navidezno obleganje virov spremeni v ovrgljivo srečanje, hitrim ljudem dovoli zavrniti ritem, ki postaji najbolj koristi, ter si prisluži varen skupni ritem, pri katerem aritmetika, soglasje in človeške posledice ostanejo vidni.
